source.title: Deep Residual Learning in Spiking Neural Networks
source.authors: Wei Fang; Zhaofei Yu; Yanqi Chen; Tiejun Huang; Timothée Masquelier; Yonghong Tian

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendix.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares training loss and accuracy across spiking network depths and residual block designs, addressing the depth and shortcut portion of V3 in a different network family.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training-loss and training-accuracy comparisons for Spiking ResNet, SEW ResNet, and plain networks. Firing-rate and gradient plots are not separate rows because they do not measure the training outcome named by the claim versions. Comparisons with prior work in Tables 3, 5, and 6 are cited results, not this study’s own runs.
record.test_reason: The ImageNet depth sweep tests the extension of V3 to batch-normalized spiking convolutional networks: conventional spiking residual blocks degrade with depth, whereas SEW blocks that preserve identity and gradient transmission improve. It does not replicate the plain ANN comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion: conventional Spiking ResNet blocks suffer degradation, while SEW blocks enable identity mapping and improved training with depth. The demonstrated depth sweep is on ImageNet; DVS Gesture and CIFAR10-DVS provide other performance comparisons, not independent depth sweeps.
record.recipe_differences: Direct surrogate-gradient training of spiking neural networks; compares standard spiking residual blocks, SEW blocks, and plain blocks. Uses SGD with momentum and, for ImageNet, zero initialization for the reported Spiking ResNet runs.
record.method_sensitivity: On ImageNet, reported Spiking ResNet results use zero initialization because deeper variants did not converge without it. On DVS Gesture, training-loss ordering differs by block design; SEW AND has the highest loss and SEW IAND the lowest.

fits_no_version.finding: DVS Gesture training loss ranks SEW IAND, Spiking ResNet, SEW ADD, Plain Net, then SEW AND, from lowest to highest.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At fixed depth, spiking block design and its tuned training recipe affect optimization; training loss and test accuracy can rank architectures differently.

fits_no_version.finding: Changing surrogate gradients substantially changes CIFAR-10 test accuracy; Constant 1 gives 12.56% for SEW and 10% for Spiking ResNet.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Avoiding the analyzed gradient multiplication problem alone does not guarantee successful surrogate-gradient training of residual SNNs.

fits_no_version.finding: Random temporal delete raises training loss and lowers training accuracy while improving test accuracy on DVS Gesture.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Temporal data augmentation can increase training difficulty while reducing overfitting in SNNs.

record.problems: The training-loss curves in Figure 3 do not provide numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The DVS Gesture comparison reports loss ordering across block types, not a depth sweep.
record.rows_left_out: No reported outcome matching the claim versions was omitted. Comparisons against prior studies in Tables 3, 5, and 6 were left out because they are cited results, not this study’s own experiments.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in conventional CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 convolutional networks, including random labels, size effects, and regularization.
ReLU teacher-student local minima and the effect of adding student neurons.
The plain ANN depth comparison, persistence after longer training, CIFAR-10 depth sweeps, very deep plain tanh networks, and Fixup without normalization.

Activation-matched initialization in plain networks, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and trainable depth of plain convolutional networks. The initialization experiments here concern residual SNNs.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, curvature dynamics, recovery, and divergence.
Controlled comparisons with and without batch normalization, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.

missing.what: Training accuracy across ImageNet depths is a separate, directly relevant measure missing from the loss-only rows. The text explicitly states that SEW training accuracy increases with depth; exact curve values cannot be recovered reliably from the supplied extraction.

Spiking ResNet-50/101/152 failed to converge without zero initialization. This material condition on the reported depth results needs its own outcome rows; no numerical loss or training error is stated.
missing.locator: Section 4.1, paragraph preceding the architecture comparison

record.verdict_notes: V3 verdicts concern an extension to surrogate-gradient spiking networks, not a contradiction of the original ANN experiments. Loss trends are stated explicitly, but exact per-model training values and uncertainty are unavailable. Zero initialization means zeroing selected final BN parameters, not every network weight. Tables 3, 5, and 6 mix this study's own SEW results with cited comparison results.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, network size, and training duration.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and student width relative to teacher width.

The study tests directly trained spiking networks on ImageNet and DVS Gesture, not the stated ImageNet/CIFAR-10 batch-normalized ANN recipe. It does not test whether residual networks train without normalization using Fixup, or plain tanh networks trained with special initialization.
Activation-matched initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and 10,000-layer plain convolutional networks.
Training above stability limits, curvature or sharpness dynamics, and divergence thresholds.
Batch normalization’s speed and learning-rate effects, and Fixup training without normalization.

relationships.condition: ImageNet, conventional Spiking ResNet blocks, depths 18–152, with zero initialization
relationships.reason: R1–R5 report higher training loss with depth despite residual shortcuts; identity in the forward pass does not ensure effective gradient transmission in these SNNs.
relationships.display_finding: Training loss increased with depth despite shortcuts, and forward-pass identity did not ensure effective gradient transmission.
